subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A nerve cell (neurone) is long and has many branched connections. This adaptation allows it to:
options: Carry electrical impulses over long distances and connect to many cells
questions.explain: The length and branches let neurones transmit impulses across the body and link to many other cells.

questions.q: A root hair cell has a long projection. How does this help its function?
options: It helps the cell carry oxygen
It increases surface area for absorbing water and minerals
It allows the cell to photosynthesise
questions.explain: The long extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.

questions.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: Chloroplasts (along with cell wall and permanent vacuole) are plant-specific, while the others are common to both.

questions.q: In an osmosis investigation, a potato chip GAINED mass. This shows the solution it was in was:
options: More dilute than the cell contents
The same concentration as the cell contents
More concentrated than the cell contents
questions.explain: Gaining mass means water entered by osmosis, so the surrounding solution was more dilute than the cell contents.

questions.q: Water moves into a cell by osmosis when the cell is surrounded by a solution with:
options: The same water concentration as the cell
A lower water concentration than the cell
A higher water concentration than the cell
questions.explain: Water moves from where there is more water (more dilute solution) into the cell.

questions.q: What is the role of the permanent vacuole in a plant cell?
options: Contains cell sap to keep the cell turgid (firm)
questions.explain: The vacuole is filled with cell sap and helps keep the plant cell rigid and supported.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotic cells have genetic material not enclosed in a nucleus
Eukaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus
Prokaryotic cells are larger than eukaryotic cells
questions.explain: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus, whereas eukaryotes (plants, animals) have membrane-bound organelles including a nucleus.

questions.q: Which feature of an alveolus does NOT help gas exchange?
questions.explain: Alveoli have thin walls (short diffusion distance), not thick ones; thin walls speed up diffusion.

questions.q: In which organelle does most aerobic respiration take place?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in pure (distilled) water. What is most likely to happen to its cells?
options: Water leaves the cells and they become flaccid
Sugar diffuses out of the cells
Water enters the cells by osmosis and they become turgid
questions.explain: Pure water is more dilute than the cell contents, so water enters by osmosis, making cells turgid and increasing mass.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 30 mm long and the magnification is ×1500. What is the actual size?
questions.explain: Actual = image ÷ magnification = 30 mm ÷ 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 µm.

questions.q: Folding of a cell surface membrane (e.g. in the small intestine) speeds up absorption because it:
options: Adds more energy to the particles
Increases the surface area for exchange
questions.explain: Folds (villi/microvilli) increase surface area, increasing the rate of diffusion and active transport.
